Neighbourhood guide · Singapore

Holland Village

a town of Singapore — sights & hawker food, sourced

33 places · 3 sights · 30 to eat & drink · 1 areas · 18 sources · status last checked 2026-10-03

Holland Village

Holland Village 33

  1. Must see · Holland Village

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre

    The Holland-Ghim Moh district's great hawker centre: opened in 1978, rebuilt in a 2015 facelift and refreshed again in a March-May 2024 renovation, yet still old-school neighbourhood in feel — around 72 cooked-food stalls over a wet market, famous for chwee kueh, braised duck, hor fun and carrot cake, a short walk from Buona Vista MRT.

    Look for Hawker centre & wet market; most stalls breakfast-to-lunch, some till evening

    20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020

    Recommended by Time Out Singapore, Seth Lui, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, Ordinary Patrons

  2. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Ghim Moh Chwee Kueh

    A household name since 1959 and a Michelin Guide pick: soft-but-springy steamed rice cakes (minimum four) heaped with chye poh fried over a charcoal stove, which gives the preserved radish a smokier depth than the gas-cooked norm.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-54, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Michelin Guide, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Seth Lui

  3. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    New Lucky Claypot Rice

    Holland Drive's headline stall and a Michelin Bib Gourmand year after year (incl. 2024 and 2025): every claypot is cooked from scratch over charcoal, so the grains stay separate with a crackling crust — call ahead, because the wait can run to an hour.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-19, 44 Holland Drive, S270044

    Recommended by Michelin Guide — Bib Gourmand, Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  4. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Chuan Kee Boneless Braised Duck

    Ghim Moh's Michelin Bib Gourmand duck stall: boneless Teochew-style braised duck over rice, kway teow or congee, dressed in a dark herbal gravy whose braising stock is reused and replenished daily — a $3-$5 bowl with years of depth in it.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-04, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Michelin Guide — Bib Gourmand, Seth Lui

  5. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Ru Ji Kitchen

    A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand hawker across two adjoining stalls: noodle soup or 'dry' noodles with minced pork, pork balls or fish balls hand-made on the spot — the yellowtail fishballs are the draw.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-28/29, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Michelin Guide — Bib Gourmand

  6. Worth the detour · Holland Village

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre

    The Holland Drive estate's two-storey market and food centre, home to a Michelin Bib Gourmand claypot rice (New Lucky), a Michelin-recognised kway chap (Cheng Heng), Margaret Drive Sin Kee chicken rice and a well-loved Malay breakfast stall — the residents' hawker centre just south of the Holland V bar strip.

    Look for Hawker centre & wet market; cooked food upstairs

    44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, HungryGoWhere

  7. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Hin Fried Hor Fun

    Fried to order over a superheated wok so the flat rice noodles take on real wok hei before the gravy goes in — the brown-sauce beef hor fun is the bestseller; written up by Dr Leslie Tay and Miss Tam Chiak and tested by Seth Lui as one of Singapore's best-rated hor fun.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  8. Worth the detour · Malay & Nasi Padang · Holland Village

    Shima's Kitchen

    The Malay stall at Holland Drive that tastes like someone's mum cooked it — creamy coconut lontong and mee soto in the morning, then a changing nasi padang spread (rendang, petai, curry chicken) that sells out early.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-12, 44 Holland Drive, S270044

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, HungryGoWhere

  9. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Yuan Hokkien Fried Prawn Mee (Ghim Moh)

    A Margaret Drive Food Centre transplant: white and yellow noodles wok-fried down in a rich stock of prawn heads, squid and pork bones — one of the Ghim Moh picks shared by Women's Weekly and Her World.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  10. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Blanco Court Kueh Chap (Holland Drive)

    The kway chap stall Miss Tam Chiak calls chef Daniel Tay's favourite: silky rice sheets in a herbal braising broth with a spread of braised pork, offal and egg — written up by Daniel Food Diary, SG Food on Foot and in Eatbook's 13 best Holland Drive stalls.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-02, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, Miss Tam Chiak, SG Food on Foot

  11. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Holland Village

    Lao Chen Ji Sarawak Kolo Mee (Holland Drive)

    Springy Sarawak kolo mee, served with yong tau foo pieces — a regulars' favourite named by HungryGoWhere, Daniel Food Diary (2023), Johor Kaki and Women's Weekly.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-43, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Daniel Food Diary, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), The Singapore Women's Weekly

  12. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Holland Village

    Ghim Moh Carrot Cake

    The most popular carrot cake at Ghim Moh — a family stall that makes both the radish cake and the chye poh from scratch daily; the queue starts at 6:30am and limited portions sell out, rewarding early birds with strong wok hei.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-16, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, Ordinary Patrons

  13. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Holland Village

    Heavens (Appam & Thosai)

    Formerly Heavens Indian Curry, now a mother-and-son appam and thosai specialist: lacy-edged, pillow-centred fermented-rice appam with grated coconut and orange sugar, or the indulgent 'Princess' crowned with butter, cheddar and a fried egg.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-26, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), The Singapore Women's Weekly

  14. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Cheng Heng Kway Chap and Braised Duck Rice

    A Michelin-recognised kway chap (Michelin Plate, 2018) where the broad rice sheets swim in a herbal soy broth beside braised pork and innards, plus the stall's famous finely sliced braised duck — expect a 30-minute morning queue.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-05, 44 Holland Drive, S270044

    Recommended by Seth Lui, SG Food on Foot, Her World Singapore

  15. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Fifty Year Yong Tau Foo (Holland Drive)

    Freshly made Hakka yong tau foo over flat mee kia noodles — a fifty-year name that HungryGoWhere, Johor Kaki and Eatbook all list among Holland Drive's regulars' picks.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-37, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Eatbook.sg

  16. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Holland Village

    Ah Seng Durian (Ghim Moh)

    A durian stall trading Malaysian fruit for over 40 years — Mao Shan Wang, Black Thorn, Golden Phoenix, Red Prawn — that Time Out singles out for 'reliability and excellent durians' and Eatbook ranks among Singapore's 15 best durian stalls.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (stall to confirm)

    Recommended by Time Out Singapore, Eatbook.sg

  17. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Holland Village

    Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice

    Steamed chicken rice since 1978; on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list since 2018.

    #02-06 Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive

    Recommended by Michelin Guide, Seth Lui

  18. Deep cut · Thai · Holland Village

    Yuan Authentic Thai Stewed Beef Noodle (Ghim Moh)

    Run by a cook from Chiang Rai: Thai stewed and sliced beef noodle soup — beefy, aromatic broth, beef balls, slices and tendon, small bowls from under $3 — a Thai hawker kitchen in an otherwise Chinese-heavy centre (Eatbook review; Women's Weekly and Her World Ghim Moh lists).

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, Eatbook.sg

  19. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Jiu Jiang Shao La (Ghim Moh)

    A short-hours roast-meat counter (10am-2pm, Thursday to Sunday) for roast duck, crackling roast pork and char siew — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak and listed by Women's Weekly / Her World among Ghim Moh's best.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore

  20. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Yap Kee Wanton Egg Noodles (Holland Drive)

    Wanton mee made with egg noodles supplied by the owner's brother in Johor Bahru (Johor Kaki) — on HungryGoWhere's and Eatbook's Holland Drive lists.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Eatbook.sg

  21. Deep cut · Holland Village

    Holland Village

    A long-time bohemian expat enclave of eateries, bars and shophouses off Holland Road.

    Look for Heritage

    Lorong Mambong, Holland Village

    Recommended by Visit Singapore (Singapore Tourism Board), Wikipedia (English)

  22. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Hakka Noodle (Holland Drive)

    One of Holland Drive's busier stalls: springy Hakka noodles heaped with yong tau foo pieces and crisp fried wantons — a generous neighbourhood bowl.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-15, 44 Holland Drive, S270044

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  23. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Holland Village

    Aini Muslim Food (Holland Drive)

    Holland Drive's Malay stall for ayam penyet: fragrant rice, fried chicken, tempeh, tau kwa, cucumber and sambal from about $4.50-$5 — on both Eatbook's and Women's Weekly's Holland Drive lists.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  24. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Leong Wei Roasted Delights (Holland Drive)

    The $3 char siew and roast pork rice that Eatbook headlines in its Holland Drive guide; Women's Weekly also lists it among the centre's 10 best.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-36, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  25. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Traditional Carrot Cake (Holland Drive)

    Black or white chai tow kway in $3/$4/$5 portions — the carrot cake pick of both Eatbook and Women's Weekly at Holland Drive.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  26. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Holland Village

    Butter Town (Holland Drive)

    Young hawkers baking affordable shio pan from scratch inside a hawker centre — a newer Holland Drive draw named by Seth Lui's 11 best and covered by Eatbook.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-35, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  27. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Holland Village

    Gaziantep Delights (Holland Drive)

    Restaurant-quality Turkish food at hawker prices — tombik, döner, pide and falafel — picked by Seth Lui and HungryGoWhere.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-13, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere

  28. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Holland Village

    Zhen Ji Vegetarian (Holland Drive)

    Holland Drive's vegetarian stall, a regulars' pick on HungryGoWhere and in Daniel Food Diary's 2023 Holland Drive round-up.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Daniel Food Diary

  29. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Ru Fa Bao Dian (Holland Drive)

    A handmade-bao stall named in Daniel Food Diary's 2023 Holland Drive guide and Eatbook's 13 best Holland Drive stalls.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-09, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg

  30. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Lin Da Ma Lei Cha (Holland Drive)

    Hakka thunder tea rice with a modern twist: brown rice, chopped vegetables, peanuts and ikan bilis under a thick basil-based tea soup (Daniel Food Diary); also in Seth Lui's 11 best Holland Drive stalls.

    Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-21, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui

  31. Deep cut · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Holland Village

    Thiam Kee 1977 Hainanese Chicken Rice (Ghim Moh)

    Thick, succulent slices of steamed chicken over fragrant rice — a $5.50 set with soup and greens or bean sprouts — at Ghim Moh, picked in Seth Lui's 11 best Ghim Moh stalls and found in Daniel Food Diary's best chicken rice round-up.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-19, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  32. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Holland Village

    Teck Hin Delicacies (Ghim Moh)

    After pivoting to chee cheong fun only, this Ghim Moh stall draws queues from 6.30am — in Eatbook's 10 Ghim Moh stalls and Miss Tam Chiak's chee cheong fun round-up.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, #01-30, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  33. Closed — kept for the record · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Holland Village

    Guan Kee Fried Kway Teow — CLOSED

    Started in 1969 and at Ghim Moh since 1978, this was one of Singapore's most-queued char kway teow stalls (Bib Gourmand 2019) — it closed for good on 28 Nov 2023 when its 77-year-old owner retired after fainting at the wok. Kept here as a flagged closure.

    Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, S270020

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Mothership, Seth Lui, Wikipedia
